skill.name: architecture-navigator
skill.description: Map the DevPrep AI seven-folder architecture, recommend code locations, discover modules, and review organization against documented placement and import rules.
skill.summary: Navigate DevPrep AI structure and place new code according to its architecture rules.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: All 68 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax or expected read-only shell operations. The scanner does not write files or access the network. Semantic review found one shell injection example and one indirect prompt injection channel involving repository-controlled names.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the documented sh -c command with a loop that receives paths as positional arguments and always quotes each path.

remediation.issue: Unescaped repository names enter model context
remediation.suggestion: Escape control characters and Markdown in scanner output, then instruct the agent to treat all scanned names strictly as untrusted data.

static_findings.snippet: 6. **Types Are Global**: Put shared types in types/ to avoid circular dependencies
1. **Is it a route/page?** → `app/` (but keep minimal, import from modules/)
| "Where should social login go?" | `modules/auth/` - Feature-specific authentication logic |
| "Where should I add payment processing?" | `modules/payments/` - New feature module for payment do
| "Where do reusable buttons go?" | `shared/components/ui/Button.tsx` - Reusable UI component |
| "Where's the Claude AI integration?" | `lib/claude/` - External service integration |
| "Where should shopping cart state go?" | `store/cartStore.ts` - Global state management |
| "Where do API types go?" | `types/ai/api.ts` - Shared TypeScript definitions |
- ✅ Shared components are in `shared/`, not duplicated
1. Run `scripts/scan_architecture.sh` to generate current architecture map
The OAuth client setup (SDK wrapper) should go in `lib/oauth/client.ts` (external integration).
**Manual invocation:** Use `/architecture` or explicitly request "scan the architecture".
4. **Reference rules**: Point to `architecture-rules.md` for detailed justification
2. **Notification State** → `store/uiStore.ts` (global state for managing active toasts)

semantic_findings.title: Shell Injection Through Module Directory Names
semantic_findings.description: The module discovery example inserts find output into sh -c source text. A crafted directory name can break quoting and execute arbitrary shell commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: GNU find replaces braces inside the shell source argument. Repository-controlled quotes or command substitutions in a directory name can become executable syntax.

semantic_findings.title: Indirect Prompt Injection Through Scanner Output
semantic_findings.description: The workflow consumes scanner output, while the scanner prints repository-controlled names without escaping. Crafted names can place instruction-like text into model context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data flow from repository-controlled names to model-facing Markdown is explicit. Exploitation requires a crafted repository name and unsafe treatment of output as instructions.

content.value_statement: Developers can lose time deciding where code belongs in DevPrep AI. This skill maps the structure and applies documented placement rules.
actual_capabilities: Scans seven expected source folders and counts TypeScript and React files.
Lists feature modules, subdirectory counts, and Zustand store slices.
Identifies standard API, state, component, type, style, and route locations.
Recommends paths using documented feature, reuse, integration, state, and type rules.
Reviews import direction and folder responsibilities using documented checks.
limitations: The rules are tailored to the DevPrep AI repository and its seven-folder structure.
The scanner assumes a frontend/src directory and Unix shell utilities.
The scanner reports paths and counts but does not build a dependency graph.
Grep-based validation can miss semantic violations or report acceptable imports.

use_cases.title: Place a New Feature
use_cases.description: Choose exact folders for feature logic, reusable components, integrations, state, and shared types.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Drift
use_cases.description: Compare current modules and imports with the documented seven-folder responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Build Repository Context
use_cases.description: Generate a compact structure map before planning or implementing a development task.

prompt_templates.title: Map the Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the current DevPrep AI architecture. Summarize the seven folders, feature modules, key locations, and file counts.

prompt_templates.title: Place New Code
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to add [feature]. Recommend exact paths for its logic, UI, state, integrations, and types. Explain each placement rule.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Organization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [area] against the documented folder and import rules. List confirmed violations, evidence, and specific moves or import changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cross-Cutting Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the placement and dependency flow for [complex feature]. Separate domain code, reusable elements, external integrations, global state, and shared types.

output_examples.output: Place authentication behavior in modules/auth/oauth. Put the external OAuth client wrapper in lib/oauth because it integrates with a third-party service.

output: The repository uses seven source folders for routes, features, shared code, integrations, state, types, and styles.
The map lists each feature module with TypeScript file counts.
Key locations identify the API layer, store slices, and shared components.

output_examples.input: Where should a global toast system go?
output_examples.output: Place the reusable toast component and hook under shared. Keep application-wide toast state in store and preserve the allowed dependency direction.

best_practices: Run the scanner before recommendations when repository structure may have changed.
Provide exact paths and cite the placement rule behind every recommendation.
Verify import direction after moving code between architectural folders.
anti_patterns: Do not place business logic directly in route files.
Do not move single-use feature code into shared prematurely.
Do not allow one feature module to import another feature module directly.

faq.question: Which repositories does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets DevPrep AI repositories that use the documented seven-folder frontend structure.

faq.question: Does the scanner modify source files?
faq.answer: No. The bundled scanner enumerates local directories and prints counts and names.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. Architecture scanning and documentation lookup use local repository files.

faq.question: Can it identify circular dependencies?
faq.answer: It explains forbidden dependency directions, but it does not construct a complete dependency graph.

faq.question: Can I use it with a different folder layout?
faq.answer: The recommendations will require adapted rules because the included guidance assumes DevPrep AI conventions.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
